## TL;DR

The desktop board now applies the phone queue's `sort` and shows every
phone-only `status` value as a notice chip, so no URL value is dropped
silently at 768 or 1280 px. The phone queue keeps owning these values at 375 px.
The change is covered by jsdom cases and headless WebKit fixtures at 375, 768 and
1280 px. `repoos check --changed main` passes.

## Work and rationale

The #1257 QA pass found two gaps. A `sort=oldest` link from the phone queue did
nothing on the board. A `?status=attention|held|archived|human|all` link showed
every task with no chip. The task allowed either applying each value or showing a
notice. I did both, choosing per value:

- **Sort is applied.** A valid `sort=newest|oldest` orders every column by last
  update, the same comparator the phone queue uses. A "Sort: Oldest updated" chip
  shows it, so a sorted board never looks like the default. Absent `sort` leaves the
  board's own Sort control in charge. I moved the comparator into
  `lib/workQueueFilters.ts` as `sortWorkQueueTasks` and pointed `MobileWorkQueue`
  at it, so the two views cannot drift.
- **Status is noticed, not applied.** The board can only show the six status
  columns. Phone-only values (`attention`, `all`, `needs`, `held`, `archived`,
  `human`) and unknown values get an "Ignored filter: status=…" chip, using the
  dashed style the existing priority and mine notices use. Applying them on the board
  would have meant reimplementing the held, archived and human lists there, which is
  a larger change than this bug needs.
- **Clear covers what the bar shows.** The bar now holds the sort chip and the status
  notice, so Clear removes the URL sort and an ignored status. A board status column
  stays, because it has its own bar and "Show all statuses" link. The earlier QA
  case that kept a valid `status` still holds.
- **Dropdown and URL sort.** While a URL sort is present it overrides the board's
  Sort control. Picking a sort in that control drops the URL sort, so the control
  cannot silently do nothing.

The chip bar is rendered only in the desktop branch of `WorkView`, so the phone never
shows a notice for a value its own queue applies.

Other files: `BoardQueueFilters.vue` gained a `sort` prop, and its Clear comment was
updated. `docs/qa/2026-11-filter-persistence-qa.md` now describes the new board
behavior and no longer lists #1260 as an open gap.

## Approaches tried

I first considered applying every status value on the board, which would have
needed the held, archived and human lists there. I rejected that: the board already
has its own hidden-category toggles, so the notice is the smaller correct fix for
those values. I also considered a sort notice in place of applying the sort. The
task title asked for the queue sort to be applied, and the comparator was already
shared, so applying it was cheap.

For the sort's Clear behavior I weighed keeping `sort` out of Clear, as the earlier
QA pass had it. Without a removal path, though, an applied sort on the board could
not be undone from the bar. So Clear now removes it, and I changed the matching
comment and QA doc.

## Challenges and blockers

- The first `build:ui` failed on a type error in my test helper. The `ignored`
  prop type needed to be the exported `WorkQueueFilterChip`, not an inline object.
  Fixed; the build then passed.
- The handoff that failed was `remote validation failed: test failure: gate exit 1
  on mini`. The handoff status gives no failing test name, and I could not see the
  remote log, so I could not reproduce that exact failure.
- This session I re-ran the gate. `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check --changed
  main` passes, with the scoped test step skipped because the remote runner owns it.
  The four UI files that cover this change (`work-queue-filters`,
  `work-filter-persistence-qa-browser` with its 375/768/1280 WebKit fixtures, and
  `mobile-work-queue`) pass locally: 66 of 66.
- The full local suite (`bun run test`) ran twice. The first run had five failures
  in `handoff`, `message-queueing` and `agent-review`, all server tests. The second
  run had two: `agent-review` timed out in a `waitFor`, and `detect.test.ts` got a null
  version from a fake shell binary. Each file passes when run alone, and none imports
  the filter code. They look like load flakes, not this change. I did not confirm that
  on an idle machine, so the remote run is the real answer.
- Nothing here needs a human on a real device. Touch targets and the native shell
  remain unverified, as the QA doc already says. The 768 and 1280 px cases are
  WebKit viewport emulations, not real devices.
## Key learnings

- A URL value is only "handled" if every view that reads it either applies it or
  says so. The phone queue and the board read the same keys, so the board's
  ignored-value path is the right place to add notices, and it must not run on the
  phone, where the value is applied.
- Keeping the sort comparator in one shared function removed a copy that could drift.
  The phone queue's order is now defined in one place.
- Clear has to remove what its bar displays. Keeping a sort out of Clear would have
  left a sort with no way to remove it from the bar.
